methodOrigin.name: Strategy Canvas

primarySource.title: Strategy Canvas | Blue Ocean Strategy Tools and Frameworks

methodOrigin.sourceClaim: The Strategy Canvas is a diagnostic and action framework developed by W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne for comparing the factors, offering levels, and strategic profiles that shape a market.
methodOrigin.localAdaptation: This repository adapts the comparison form for internal collaboration. Its good-enough threshold, consequence weight, lifecycle, evidence, participant input, and AI collaboration fields are repository-specific extensions.

fourActionsFramework.name: Four Actions Framework

primarySource.title: Four Actions Framework | Blue Ocean Strategy Tools and Frameworks

fourActionsFramework.sourceClaim: The Four Actions Framework was developed by W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne to ask what to eliminate, reduce, raise, and create when shaping a new value curve.

canonical.sourceClaim: The Strategy Canvas was developed by INSEAD strategy scholars W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne as a diagnostic and action framework for Blue Ocean Strategy.
canonical.adaptationClaim: This implementation adapts the comparison form for internal collaboration. Its good-enough threshold, consequence weight, lifecycle, evidence, participant input, and AI collaboration fields are repository-specific extensions.
canonical.boundaryClaim: The 0–10 scores are locally defined comparison coordinates. Research informs the interaction and representation choices; claims about comprehension, accessibility, readiness, and decision improvement require evidence designed for those questions.

contextCanvas.sourceClaim: The Strategy Canvas was developed by INSEAD strategy scholars W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne as a diagnostic and action framework for Blue Ocean Strategy.
contextCanvas.adaptationClaim: This Context Canvas workbench adapts the comparison form for internal collaboration. Its current, good-enough, desired, consequence, evidence, participant input, scenario, and AI collaboration fields are repository-specific extensions.
contextCanvas.boundaryClaim: The local 0–10 scores support comparison. Evidence designed for decision and change outcomes establishes those claims.

narrativeCapsuleComposer.sourceClaim: The Strategy Canvas was developed by INSEAD strategy scholars W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne as a diagnostic and action framework for Blue Ocean Strategy.
narrativeCapsuleComposer.adaptationClaim: This composer adapts the comparison form through a NOW / NEXT / LATER projection.
narrativeCapsuleComposer.boundaryClaim: Its local dimensions, thresholds, evidence fields, and capsule bindings remain provisional until reviewed in their receiving context.

genomicViewer.sourceClaim: This static representation adapts the Strategy Canvas developed by W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne.
genomicViewer.adaptationClaim: It maps the ten dimensions named in the research-to-architecture trace.
genomicViewer.boundaryClaim: The action groupings are an inspectable 2026 local synthesis. Scores recorded at the time, observed outcomes, and the costing model remain separate evidence routes.

initiativeCosting.sourceClaim: The Four Actions Framework was developed by W. Chan Kim and Renée Mauborgne to ask what to eliminate, reduce, raise, and create when shaping a new value curve.
initiativeCosting.adaptationClaim: This action area uses the four categories to organize editable planning suggestions.
initiativeCosting.boundaryClaim: Market-strategy conclusions retain their own evidence and review.

implementationEvidence.citation: Shneiderman, B. (1983). Direct Manipulation: A Step Beyond Programming Languages. Computer, 16(8), 57–69.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: Marker movement and labelled score controls update the same visible state, and undo and redo preserve reversibility.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: This account motivates the interaction pattern; it does not establish usability or decision quality for this implementation.

implementationEvidence.citation: Larkin, J. H., & Simon, H. A. (1987). Why a Diagram is (Sometimes) Worth Ten Thousand Words. Cognitive Science, 11(1), 65–100.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: The plotted profile and a complete structured table remain adjacent semantic twins.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The paper analyzes when informationally equivalent diagrams can make lookup and inference more efficient; it does not show that a diagram is always easier to understand.

implementationEvidence.citation: W3C Web Accessibility Initiative. Complex Images tutorial.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: Each complex chart has a short description and a visible, structured long-form table equivalent.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The guidance shapes the text-equivalent route; conformance and practical access still require testing with relevant users and technologies.

implementationEvidence.citation: Cleveland, W. S., & McGill, R. (1984). Graphical Perception: Theory, Experimentation, and Application to the Development of Graphical Methods. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 79(387), 531–554.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: Scores use position on a common aligned scale, with exact values repeated in marker labels and tables.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The experiments compare elementary graphical judgments. They do not validate this curve, its local scale, or its decision meaning.

implementationEvidence.citation: Heer, J., & Shneiderman, B. (2012). Interactive Dynamics for Visual Analysis. Communications of the ACM, 55(4), 45–54.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: Selection, filtering by attention, direct value change, and state inspection remain explicit and reversible across chart and native controls.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The taxonomy supports interaction design choices; it is not an evaluation of this artifact or its audience.

implementationEvidence.citation: Lorenz, J., Rauhut, H., Schweitzer, F., & Helbing, D. (2011). How social influence can undermine the wisdom of crowd effect. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 108(22), 9020–9025.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: The Context Canvas adaptation can collect independent participant readings before an explicit reveal.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The experiment used factual estimation tasks with 144 participants. Its result does not establish a universal benefit for concealed entry or apply directly to every collaboration task.

counterevidence.citation: Farrell, S. (2011). Social influence benefits the wisdom of individuals in the crowd. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 108(36), E625.
counterevidence.relevance: This response argues that social information can improve individual estimates, reinforcing a context-dependent rather than universal interpretation.

implementationEvidence.citation: Weiner, B. J. (2009). A theory of organizational readiness for change. Implementation Science, 4, 67.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: Local dimensions may separately name shared commitment, capability, resources, and situational conditions when they matter to a change decision.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The paper presents a theory and calls for further measurement development. This Strategy Canvas does not measure organizational readiness unless a separate validated method is supplied.

implementationEvidence.citation: Treisman, A. M., & Gelade, G. (1980). A feature-integration theory of attention. Cognitive Psychology, 12(1), 97–136.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: The current dimension is identified by visible text and a persistent border treatment as well as color.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The experiments concern attention to separable visual features. They motivate redundancy but do not establish accessibility or comprehension for this control.

implementationEvidence.citation: Tversky, A., & Kahneman, D. (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science, 185(4157), 1124–1131.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: Every number remains attached to local observable anchors and an evidence field, with participant spread retained where available.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: Visible anchors and evidence make interpretation inspectable; they do not remove anchoring effects or other judgment biases.

implementationEvidence.citation: Kim, W. C., & Mauborgne, R. Four Actions Framework. Blue Ocean Strategy Tools and Frameworks.
implementationEvidence.implementationDecision: The initiative-costing action area names the framework's four categories and states how the local planning adaptation uses them.
implementationEvidence.transferLimit: The official description establishes the method origin. Local planning suggestions and market-strategy conclusions retain their own evidence routes.

claimBoundaries: The repository-specific 0–10 scales are locally defined rather than psychometrically validated.
The Strategy Canvas shows authored and derived readings; it does not determine whether a strategy or change will succeed.
Cognitive and interaction research informs specific design choices without proving universal comprehension, accessibility, or decision improvement.
